content.text: {"title":"Hello, Click: one value's round trip through a command line","premise":"A caller has a Python function, `hello(count, name)`, and wants it to behave like a real command line program: `--count=3` typed on the command line, a name asked for interactively, output captured so a test can assert on it. Nothing in the function knows about argv, prompts, encodings, or exit codes. The data that arrives — the argument list `['--count=3']` and the keystrokes `'Click\\n'` — has to cross from an untrusted outside world into a typed Python call, and a result has to come back out with an exit code that means something. This is the story of that crossing, and of the guarantees Click makes along the way.","chapters":[{"n":1,"title":"Before the data: declarations become objects","trace_lines":[2,38],"data_in":"the undecorated function `hello` plus decorator keywords: `default=1, help=\"Number of greetings.\"` and `prompt=\"Your name\", help=\"The person to greet.\"`","data_out":"`<Command hello>` carrying `params=[<Option count>, <Option name>]`, each with a resolved name, type and default","code":["src/click/decorators.py:352-377","src/click/decorators.py:314-321","src/click/decorators.py:168-255","src/click/core.py:3055-3131","src/click/core.py:2356-2438","src/click/core.py:3355-3420","src/click/core.py:3155-3186","src/click/core.py:3188-3225","src/click/core.py:3251-3271","src/click/types.py:1311-1397"],"inputs":["--count=3"],"characters":["option","_param_memo","command","Option.__init__","Parameter.__init__","Option._parse_decls","Option._infer_flag_kind","Option._pick_type","Option._validate","convert_type","_guess_type","UNSET"],"facts":["`option()` builds an `Option` immediately and stashes it on `f.__click_params__`; `command()` pops that list, reverses it, and hands it to `Command(name='hello', callback=hello, params=[...])`, so declaration order in the source is the order in `Command.params`.","`--name` has no explicit `default`, so `Parameter.__init__` stores the sentinel `UNSET` and records `_default_explicit = False`. The sentinel is how Click later distinguishes \"the user never supplied a default\" from \"the default is None\".","Type is inferred, not required: `convert_type(None, UNSET)` falls through `_guess_type` to `STRING` for `--name`; the collapsed `--count` declaration passes `default=1`, so `_guess_type` returns `int` and the type becomes `INT`.","`_infer_flag_kind(is_flag=None, flag_value=UNSET)` returns `(False, False)` for `--name`: no flag_value, no secondary opts, `prompt_required` left at True, so it is an ordinary value option.","`_parse_decls` derives the Python name from the longest declaration: `'--name'` becomes `name`. `_check_name_is_usable` warns (DeprecationWarning, not an error) if that name is a Python keyword or not an identifier — a name that will become a `TypeError` in Click 9.0.","`_validate` runs only under `__debug__`; running Python with `-O` silences the illegal-combination checks (`nargs=-1` on an option, secondary flags on a non-boolean, `count` with `multiple`)."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q1.1","question":"`--name` ended up with a STRING type, no default, and a prompt string. Who turns that into an actual value, and what happens if nobody types anything?"},{"id":"q1.2","question":"`--count` was declared with `default=1` and type INT, but the command line will hand over the characters `'3'`. Where does the string become an integer, and what if it can't?"}],"answers":[]},{"n":2,"title":"An isolated world: the runner swaps the process out from under you","trace_lines":[39,57],"data_in":"`input='Click\\n'`, `env=None`, `color=False`","data_out":"three byte buffers `(stdout, stderr, output)` and a process whose `sys.stdin/stdout/stderr`, `termui` prompt hooks, `should_strip_ansi`, `pdb.Pdb.__init__` and `FORCED_WIDTH` have all been replaced","code":["src/click/testing.py:360-380","src/click/testing.py:398-594","src/click/testing.py:211-228","src/click/testing.py:117-153","src/click/testing.py:156-208"],"inputs":["Click\\n"],"characters":["CliRunner","CliRunner.isolation","make_input_stream","StreamMixer","BytesIOCopy","_NamedTextIOWrapper","visible_input","hidden_input"],"facts":["`make_input_stream` turns `'Click\\n'` into a `BytesIO`; `sys.stdin` becomes a `_NamedTextIOWrapper` over it, so the command's prompt reads from the test's string rather than a terminal.","`StreamMixer` gives stdout and stderr their own `BytesIOCopy`, each mirroring every write into a third shared buffer. That third buffer is what `Result.output` exposes, so interleaving reflects actual write order, not a post-hoc concatenation.","Default `capture='sys'` captures Python-level writes only. `_NamedTextIOWrapper.fileno()` keeps raising `io.UnsupportedOperation` (its `_original_fd` stays `-1`), which deliberately prevents user code doing `os.dup2(sys.stdout.fileno(), ...)` from clobbering the host test runner's stdout. `capture='fd'` opts into real fd redirection and is rejected on Windows.","Everything swapped is process-global: `sys.std*`, `os.environ` keys, `termui.visible_prompt_func`, `_compat.should_strip_ansi`, `pdb.Pdb.__init__`. The class docstring states this only works single-threaded; parallelism must be by process.","Environment overrides are recorded into `old_env` before mutation and restored in a `finally`, including deleting keys that were absent before.","`pdb.Pdb.__init__` is patched so a `breakpoint()` inside the command talks to `sys.__stdin__/__stdout__` (the real terminal) instead of the capture buffers. Debuggers that do not subclass `pdb.Pdb` are not covered."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q2.1","question":"All of this global state is swapped before the command runs. If the command raises — or calls `sys.exit` — does the process get its streams, env and prompt hooks back?"},{"id":"q2.2","question":"Three buffers were created. What guarantees the mixed `output` buffer shows things in the order a user at a terminal would have seen them?"}],"answers":[]},{"n":3,"title":"main(): the policy at the door","trace_lines":[58,60],"data_in":"`args=['--count=3']`, `prog_name='hello'`, `standalone_mode=True`","data_out":"an untouched arg list, a completion check that found nothing, and control handed to `make_context` inside a layered `try`","code":["src/click/core.py:1511,1562-1645","src/click/core.py:1647,1665-1677"],"inputs":["--count=3"],"characters":["Command.main","Command._main_shell_completion","Exit","Abort","ClickException","_PacifyFlushWrapper","_echo_aborted"],"facts":["`args` was given explicitly, so `sys.argv[1:]` is not read and Windows glob/env expansion (`_expand_args`) is skipped; that expansion only happens when `args is None` and `os.name == 'nt'`.","Before any parsing, `_main_shell_completion` reads the environment variable `_HELLO_COMPLETE` (derived from `prog_name`, with `-` and `.` mapped to `_`). If that variable is set, Click runs the completion machinery and calls `sys.exit` — the program never reaches its own logic. This is a real trust boundary: an attacker-controlled environment can divert the invocation.","`standalone_mode=True` (the default) is the contract that `main` never returns normally: every path ends in `sys.exit`. With `standalone_mode=False`, exceptions propagate to the caller and the invoke return value comes back instead.","Each handler in the ladder does the same two things: re-raise when not standalone, otherwise set `report` (a callable that writes the message) and `exit_code`; the writing and exiting happen once, after the `try`.","`exit_code` is initialised to `1`, so any path that sets a message but no code reports failure. An `OSError` with `errno == EPIPE` is swallowed by wrapping `sys.stdout/stderr` in `_PacifyFlushWrapper`; any other `OSError` is re-raised."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q3.1","question":"If the command succeeds, what exit code does the caller see, and who raises the `SystemExit` that produces it?"},{"id":"q3.2","question":"`--count=3` happens to be valid. Automatic env reading only turns on when the caller opts in by passing a prefix.","`Context.scope(cleanup=False)` bumps `_depth` before entering, so the matching `__exit__` cannot run the close callbacks: resources opened during parsing (a `click.File` argument, say) stay open for the command body.","The context is pushed onto a `threading.local` stack; `get_current_context()` and therefore `pass_context`, `echo`'s colour default, and `resolve_color_default` all read from that stack."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q4.1","question":"Parsing registers close callbacks on the context's ExitStack but is told not to clean up. When does anything actually get closed?"}],"answers":[]},{"n":5,"title":"Building the parser, and the help option nobody declared","trace_lines":[70,124],"data_in":"the fresh context and `args=['--count=3']`","data_out":"an `_OptionParser` with `--count`, `--name` and `--help` registered, and `Command.params` now holding a cached third option named `_click_default_help`","code":["src/click/core.py:1392-1396","src/click/core.py:1252-1257","src/click/core.py:1128-1182","src/click/core.py:1203-1250","src/click/core.py:3422-3462","src/click/decorators.py:603-627","src/click/parser.py:265-296"],"inputs":[],"characters":["Command.parse_args","Command.make_parser","Command.get_params","Command.get_help_option_names","Command.get_help_option","help_option","show_help","Option.add_to_parser","_OptionParser.add_option","_Option"],"facts":["`get_help_option_names` starts from `ctx.help_option_names` and removes any name already claimed by a user parameter, so declaring your own `-h/--help` silently suppresses the automatic one instead of colliding.","The automatic help option stores its value under the reserved name `_click_default_help`, which is why a user parameter literally named `help` no longer breaks parsing (`_HELP_OPTION_STORAGE_NAME`, core.py:61).","The help option object is cached in `Command._help_option` because `iter_params_for_processing` sorts by object identity; recreating it per call would break callback ordering.","`get_params` also runs the duplicate-name policing: a repeated option spelling, a user parameter squatting on the reserved help name, or an `Argument` sharing a storage name with another parameter each raise a `UserWarning`. Types are a higher layer entirely.","`state.order` records parameters in the order the user mentioned them. That list, not the declaration list, drives callback ordering later.","Roads not taken, all visible in this code: a bare `--` returns early and stops option parsing; an unknown long option raises `NoSuchOption` with `difflib` close matches unless `ignore_unknown_options` pushes it into leftovers; an option that needs a value but sees the next token starting with a prefix yields the `FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE` sentinel if `_flag_needs_value`, otherwise raises `BadOptionUsage`.","`parse_args` swallows `UsageError` entirely when `ctx.resilient_parsing` is set — the mode shell completion runs in. In normal operation it propagates.","With no positional parameters declared, `_unpack_args([], [])` returns `((), [])` and there are no leftover args."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[]},{"n":7,"title":"Deciding who goes first","trace_lines":[147,157],"data_in":"invocation order `[<Option count>]`, declaration order `[count, name, _click_default_help]`","data_out":"processing order `[<Option _click_default_help>, <Option count>, <Option name>]`","code":["src/click/core.py:1399","src/click/core.py:168-192"],"inputs":[],"characters":["iter_params_for_processing","sort_key","Option.is_eager"],"facts":["The sort key is `(not is_eager, index-in-invocation-order)`, with `float('inf')` for parameters the user never mentioned. Parameters that were absent still get processed, which is what makes a missing-value prompt or a default-from-another-parameter callback possible."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[]},{"n":8,"title":"The help option that was never passed","trace_lines":[158,215],"data_in":"`opts={'count': '3'}` and the help option, which appears nowhere in it","data_out":"`(None, [])` — value `False`, source `DEFAULT`, callback invoked and did nothing, `ctx.params` untouched","code":["src/click/core.py:2835-2921","src/click/core.py:3726-3780","src/click/core.py:2586-2632","src/click/core.py:3654-3676","src/click/core.py:2774-2817","src/click/core.py:3295-3327","src/click/core.py:3227-3249","src/click/core.py:3782-3797","src/click/core.py:2708-2772","src/click/decorators.py:612-616","src/click/core.py:149-166"],"inputs":[],"characters":["Parameter.handle_parse_result","Option.consume_value","Parameter.consume_value","Option.value_from_envvar","Option.resolve_envvar_value","Option.get_default","_resolve_lazy_default","Option.process_value","BoolParamType","show_help","augment_usage_errors","ParameterSource"],"facts":["`consume_value` establishes a fixed precedence, most explicit first: command line, then environment variable, then `ctx.default_map`, then the parameter's own default. Resolving lazily here (rather than in `__init__`) is what keeps `default is UNSET` a reliable answer to \"did the author pass a default?\".","The callback runs even though the user never passed `--help`: `show_help` receives `value=False` and returns immediately. The same shape guards `version_option`, which also returns early under `ctx.resilient_parsing` so completion never prints a version.","The result is discarded: `expose_value=False` means the winner of the slot arbitration does not write `ctx.params`, so the function signature never has to mention `_click_default_help`.","`handle_parse_result` arbitrates when several parameters share a storage name (feature switches): a more explicit source wins; on a tie, an explicitly-set default beats an auto-derived one; a loser's source is restored so later lookups stay truthful.","`augment_usage_errors` wraps the whole block, attaching `ctx` and `param` to any `BadParameter`/`UsageError` raised inside — that is how a type failure in a callback still reports which option caused it.","In `resilient_parsing` mode a conversion failure here is swallowed and the value reset to `UNSET`, so an invalid value cannot stop `--help` or shell completion from working."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[{"id":"q5.1","answer":"The injected help option is evaluated on every run: envvar lookup, default resolution, a `BoolParamType` conversion of `False`, and a callback call that returns at once. The cost is a handful of calls and no observable effect, because `expose_value=False` keeps it out of `ctx.params`."}]},{"n":9,"title":"The caller's '3' and the user's 'Click'","trace_lines":[216,217],"data_in":"`opts={'count': '3'}`, and for `--name` nothing at all","data_out":"`ctx.params == {'count': 3, 'name': 'Click'}`; `parse_args` returns `[]` leftovers","code":["src/click/core.py:3726-3780","src/click/core.py:3604-3652","src/click/core.py:2634-2688","src/click/core.py:2708-2772","src/click/core.py:1400-1426","src/click/types.py:593-610","src/click/testing.py:474-483"],"inputs":["--count=3","Click\\n"],"characters":["Option.consume_value","Option.prompt_for_value","prompt","visible_input","Parameter.type_cast_value","IntParamType","StringParamType","MissingParameter","ParameterSource.PROMPT","ParameterSource.COMMANDLINE"],"facts":["`--count` is found in `opts`, so its source is `COMMANDLINE` and `type_cast_value` runs `IntParamType` on `'3'`, producing `3`. Had the token been `'x'`, `_NumberParamTypeBase.convert` would have called `fail`, raising `BadParameter` — a `UsageError` subclass with `exit_code = 2`.","`--name` is absent from `opts`, has no envvar, no default map entry, and its default is still `UNSET`. Because `prompt` is set, `prompt_required` is True and `resilient_parsing` is False, `consume_value` calls `prompt_for_value` and records the source as `PROMPT`.","`prompt_for_value` computes the default *before* any interaction, then calls `termui.prompt` with `value_proc=lambda x: self.process_value(ctx, x)` — so the parameter's type and callback validate prompted input exactly as they validate command line input, and an invalid answer re-asks rather than crashing.","Under isolation, `termui.visible_prompt_func` is the runner's `visible_input`: it writes the prompt to the captured stdout, reads one line from the `BytesIO` stdin, echoes it back, and strips the newline. That is why the expected output begins with `Your name: Click`.","If stdin were exhausted, `visible_input` raises `EOFError`; `main`'s handler turns `EOFError`/`KeyboardInterrupt` into a blank line on stderr plus `Aborted!` and a non-zero exit. A prompting option therefore fails loudly, not silently, in a non-interactive pipeline.","Had `--name` had no prompt and no default, `process_value` would have raised `MissingParameter` instead; with `prompt` and `resilient_parsing` set (completion), the prompt is skipped entirely.","After all parameters are processed, `parse_args` sweeps `ctx.params` and rewrites any remaining `UNSET` to `None`, so the sentinel is never visible to user code. With nothing to read, the prompt raises `EOFError` and the run aborts with a non-zero exit code."},{"id":"q1.2","answer":"`Parameter.type_cast_value` applies the inferred `IntParamType` to the parser's raw `'3'`, yielding `3`. That is the reason parameter names must be valid Python identifiers, and why a name like `from` is only reachable through `**kwargs`.","`augment_usage_errors(self)` wraps the callback call, so a `UsageError` raised inside user code still carries the context and prints usage.","When `invoke` is handed a `Command` rather than a plain callable, it builds a sub-context and fills every missing parameter from `get_default`, mapping `UNSET` to `None` because the sentinel is deliberately kept out of the public API."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[{"id":"q4.1","answer":"Nothing closes at the end of parsing: `scope(cleanup=False)` keeps `_depth` above zero. The rewrap path exists for the ASCII-encoding case, where Click deliberately forces UTF-8 with `errors='replace'` — mojibake instead of a crash.","Colour handling is a default with teeth: `color=None` consults `resolve_color_default`, which reads `ctx.color` (None here), and then `should_strip_ansi`. Normally that answers \"strip unless `isatty()`\", so piping output removes ANSI codes; here the runner's patched version answers True because `color=False` was requested.","`echo` always flushes, and routes `bytes`/`bytearray` to the underlying binary writer when one can be found, so writing bytes to a text stream works instead of raising.","`BytesIOCopy.write` writes to the shared mixed buffer *before* its own, and `flush` flushes both — that is the mechanism behind faithful stdout/stderr interleaving.","If no standard stream exists at all (pythonw on Windows), `echo` returns silently rather than raising."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[{"id":"q2.2","answer":"Every write to the captured stdout or stderr goes through `BytesIOCopy.write`, which first appends the same bytes to the single shared `output` buffer. Ordering in `Result.output` is therefore the real write order across both streams, including the prompt echo that `visible_input` wrote before the three greetings."}]},{"n":12,"title":"Exit is an exception","trace_lines":[281,295],"data_in":"the callback's return value `None`, discarded; `ctx.exit(0)`","data_out":"`Exit(0)` raised, the ExitStack unwound with the exception info, caught by `main`, `sys.exit(0)`","code":["src/click/core.py:845-853","src/click/core.py:715-738","src/click/core.py:580-592","src/click/exceptions.py:366-378","src/click/core.py:1589-1645","src/click/exceptions.py:35-111"],"inputs":[],"characters":["Context.exit","Context.close","Context._close_with_exception_info","Exit","Context.__exit__","ClickException.show","UsageError.show","_echo_aborted"],"facts":["The return value of the command is deliberately *not* used as the exit code. The comment at core.py:1591-1597 spells out why: a callback returning `1`, or a chained group returning `[None, None]`, would make truthiness a misleading success signal. Success is always `ctx.exit()` with code 0.","`ctx.exit` closes the context *before* raising `Exit`, so `call_on_close` callbacks and `with_resource` context managers run even on an early exit (changed in 8.2).","`Context.__exit__` forwards the live exception type, value and traceback into `ExitStack.__exit__`, so a registered resource can observe and even suppress the failure; its return value becomes the `with` block's result.
